title: The Pig and the Sheep
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Pig found his way into a meadow where a flock of Sheep were grazing. The shepherd caught him, and was proceeding to carry him off to the butcher's when he set up a loud squealing and struggled to get free. The Sheep rebuked him for making such a to-do, and said to him, "The shepherd catches us regularly and drags us off just like that, and we don't make any fuss." "No, I dare say not," replied the Pig, "but my case and yours are altogether different: he only wants you for wool, but he wants me for bacon."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the Pig find his way?
options: Into a barn full of hay
Into a meadow where a flock of Sheep were grazing

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who caught the Pig?
According to the passage, what did the Pig do when he was caught?
options: He set up a loud squealing and struggled to get free
He tried to bargain with the shepherd

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Sheep say they never do when the shepherd catches them?
According to the Pig, what does the shepherd want the Sheep for?
As the passage uses it, what does "to-do" mean in "rebuked him for making such a to-do"?
Based on the passage, why does the Pig say his case and the Sheep's case are "altogether different"?
options: Because he is bigger and heavier than the Sheep
Because being caught means his death, while it costs the Sheep only their wool
Because he has never been caught before
Because the shepherd dislikes pigs more than sheep

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: It is foolish to ever protest when caught by someone stronger
Sheep are wiser than pigs in every situation
How calmly one faces danger should depend on what is actually at stake
Squealing loudly always frightens away danger

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the shepherd proceeding to carry the Pig?
According to the passage, how often does the shepherd catch the Sheep, in their own words?
According to the passage, what does the Pig say he is wanted for?
As the passage uses it, what does "rebuked" mean in "The Sheep rebuked him"?
Based on the passage, what do the Sheep seem to misunderstand about the Pig's alarm?
options: They think he is exaggerating for attention
They assume his situation carries the same low risk as their own
They believe he is afraid of the meadow itself
They think he wants to escape being sheared

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Pig is caught and calmly accepts his fate like the Sheep around him
A Pig struggles and squeals when caught, explaining to the scolding Sheep that death, not shearing, awaits him
A Pig persuades the shepherd to release him unharmed
The Sheep help the Pig escape from the shepherd
